data.title: France and UK urged to press Israel on Palestinian territories
data.description: PARIS - Dozens of former French and UK diplomats on Saturday urged their governments to work together to uphold international law in the Palestinian territories, accusing Israel of seeking to “destroy” any prospect of a viable Palestinian state.

data.title: Dozens more civilians killed, kidnapped in Nigeria
data.description: JOS, Nigeria - Jihadists kidnapped and killed scores of people in an attack during Friday prayers in central Nigeria’s Niger state, survivors and lawmakers told AFP on Saturday, though some were able to escape during a clash with rival militants.

data.title: Ukraine strikes kill two children after Russia’s deadly mall attack
data.description: KYIV - A Ukrainian drone attack on Saturday hit a house in southern Russia, killing two children and injuring their parents, officials said, while at least nine people remained missing after a Russian attack on a Ukrainian shopping centre.

data.title: Airstrike on Myanmar monastery kills 14
data.description: A Myanmar military airstrike on a monastery where civilians were gathered for a meditation retreat marking Buddhist Lent has killed 14 people, two rebel fighters who witnessed the aftermath said.

data.title: Cities compete to be Japan’s ‘backup capital’
data.description: TOKYO — For 158 years, Tokyo has stood as Japan’s glittering capital, a world-famous nexus of food, culture, business and government.

data.title: Judge strikes down Trump’s 75-country visa ban
data.description: A US federal judge has struck down the Trump administration’s ban on issuing visas to immigrants from 75 countries including Thailand, finding that the policy was “contrary to law” and beyond the legal authority of Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

data.title: TikTok to pay $400 mn settlement in US children's privacy case
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO (UNITED STATES) - TikTok and parent company ByteDance have agreed to pay $400 million to settle a lawsuit with the US Department of Justice over claims that the video-sharing platform violated federal children's privacy laws, the department announced on Friday.

data.title: Ukraine says 'cynical' Russian strike on shopping centre killed 14
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Russian drones slammed into a busy shopping centre in eastern Ukraine Friday, killing 14 people in an attack condemned as "cynical and despicable" by President Volodymyr Zelensky.

data.title: Mexican governor wanted on US drug charges returns to job
data.description: MEXICO CITY - The governor of Mexico's violence-plagued Sinaloa state, who is wanted by the United States on drug trafficking charges announced Friday he had resumed office after a nearly four-month absence to fight the allegations.

data.title: Prince Harry, others ordered to pay Daily Mail £9.5 million
data.description: LONDON - A British court ordered Prince Harry and six others on Friday to pay an initial £9.5 million ($13 million) after they lost their privacy case against the publisher of the Daily Mail.

data.title: Sword-wielding man injures several at Swedish school
data.description: STOCKHOLM - A man armed with a sword injured several people at a Swedish high school on Friday and one person was later detained, local ​authorities said.

data.title: Pope to visit San Marino, address Italian political event
data.description: VATICAN CITY - Pope Leo XIV will travel to the tiny republic of San Marino on Saturday before attending a cultural and political event organised by an influential Catholic group at an Italian seaside resort.

data.title: Romania holding suspect linked to weapons cache in Germany
data.description: BERLIN - Romania is holding a suspected “low-level agent” accused of preparing attacks, following the discovery of handguns and ammunition in a forest near Berlin, Germany’s interior minister said Friday.

data.title: Iran wants to end war while in a ‘position of strength’
data.description: TEHRAN - Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Friday it was time to end the months-long Middle East war with the United States because Tehran appeared to be in a stronger position than Washington.

data.title: ICC head warns against ‘demise of international rule of law’
data.description: TOKYO - International Criminal Court President Tomoko Akane of Japan warned on Friday against “the demise of international rule of law” after the United States targeted her with sanctions.

data.title: Ebola ‘growing exponentially’ in DR Congo
data.description: GENEVA - The Ebola outbreak raging in the Democratic Republic of Congo is growing “exponentially”, with more than 2,500 deaths recorded and half of those in the last 20 days, the senior UN coordinator on the disease said on Friday.

data.title: Indian court orders new steps to protect elephants
data.description: NEW DELHI - India’s top court has ordered tough new steps to protect wild elephant herds as habitat loss and human-elephant conflict intensify, a move welcomed by campaigners on Friday.

data.title: Australia charges man with trying to pass Ukraine military intel to Russia
data.description: SYDNEY - Australian police charged a man with foreign interference on Friday for allegedly seeking to pass intelligence about Ukrainian military activities to Russia.

data.title: Ex-Pakistan PM Khan taken back to jail after hospital checks
data.description: ISLAMABAD — Former Pakistan prime minister Imran Khan was transferred back to jail early on Friday, hours after being taken to a hospital for court-ordered medical checks, the government said.

data.title: 153,000 students and school staff affected in Canvas data breach
data.description: More than 153,000 students and staff from four tertiary institutions in Hong Kong have been affected by a data breach on the online learning management platform Canvas, an investigation by the city's privacy watchdog has found.
